learnerTasks.prompt: Given P(A) = 5/10 and P(B | A) = 7/10, find P(A and B) in lowest terms.
A trial succeeds with probability 3/10 and is repeated 2 times independently. Let X count the successes. Find P(X = 0) as a decimal.
From 7 distinct items, how many ways are there to choose 3 when the order does not matter?
A random variable takes values 2, 2, 6 with probabilities 3/10, 5/10, 2/10 respectively. Find its expected value.
Given P(A) = 8/10 and P(B | A) = 8/10, find P(A and B) in lowest terms.
A trial succeeds with probability 5/10 and is repeated 3 times independently. Let X count the successes. Find P(X = 0) as a decimal.
From 8 distinct items, how many ways are there to choose 4 when the order does not matter?
A random variable takes values 1, 15, 19, 20 with probabilities 5/10, 2/10, 2/10, 1/10 respectively. Find its expected value.
Given P(A) = 8/10 and P(B | A) = 9/10, find P(A and B) in lowest terms.
A trial succeeds with probability 1/10 and is repeated 2 times independently. Let X count the successes. Find P(X = 0) as a decimal.
From 9 distinct items, how many ways are there to choose 4 when the order does not matter?
A random variable takes values 18, 4, 16, 1 with probabilities 3/10, 5/10, 1/10, 1/10 respectively. Find its expected value.
